args.body:
REDLINE REVIEW MEMORANDUM
funds-asset-management analyze: Analyze Counterparty Markup of Investment Advisory Agreement
Matter File 15 — FUNDS ASSET MANAGEMENT

TO: Engagement File (Funds Asset Management Matter)
FROM: Deal Team / Analysis
DATE: [Current Date]
RE: Redline Review of Counterparty Markup of Investment Advisory Agreement against Standard Form and Internal Playbook

This memorandum presents a comprehensive redline review of the counterparty's markup of the investment advisory agreement, reconciling every deviation against the firm-standard form, the disclosed schedules and exhibits, and the governing deal-team instruction. The counterparty's revision accepts most firm-standard provisions, but introduces three material deviations. Each is analyzed below against the base materials, the operative disclosure schedules (which control over general statements in the base materials), and the controlling correspondence.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

The counterparty markup introduces the following deviations from the standard form:

1. A reduction of the indemnification cap, bundled with conversion of the indemnity basket from a deductible to a tipping basket;
2. New carve-outs in the definition of Material Adverse Effect ("MAE") for regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this matter; and
3. A new limitation period shortening the survival of the core representations.

Pursuant to the controlling deal-team instruction (which supersedes all earlier messages in the correspondence thread), the client will (a) CONCEDE the basket conversion, but (b) treats any survival-period reduction as a WALK-AWAY issue. Accordingly:
- The basket conversion (deductible to tipping) is ACCEPTED, but only on a stand-alone basis — it does not carry the cap reduction with it.
- The MAE carve-outs and the indemnification cap reduction are REJECTED, each for independent reasons grounded in the schedules.
- The survival-period reduction is a WALK-AWAY issue and must be withdrawn in full; it contradicts Exhibit B's survival matrix and is a term the client will not accept.

SECTION-BY-SECTION ANALYSIS

I. INDEMNIFICATION CHANGES (Cap Reduction; Basket Deductible-to-Tipping Conversion)

Deviations. The counterparty silently (a) reduces the indemnification cap and (b) converts the indemnity basket from a deductible to a tipping basket.

Base Provision / Standard Form. The firm-standard form provides a defined indemnification cap and an indemnity basket operating as a deductible (i.e., the indemnitor is not liable until losses exceed the basket, and once exceeded, liability attaches only to the excess).

Disclosure Schedule 5.2. Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that the markup's indemnification changes would silently shift. The cap reduction, in particular, would move qualifying losses above the reduced cap onto the client's retained-liability side without any adjustment to consideration or the risk allocation otherwise struck in the schedules.

Deal-Team Instruction. The controlling correspondence states the client will concede the basket conversion, but does not concede any change to the cap. Only the basket conversion is within the concession; the cap reduction is not.

Reconciliation and Recommendation:
- Basket conversion (deductible to tipping basket): ACCEPT per the governing instruction. Under a tipping basket, once aggregate losses reach the basket threshold, the indemnitor becomes liable for all losses from the first dollar. This is a reasonable commercial term the client has agreed to concede. No further negotiation required, and no pricing/consideration adjustment applies on the basis of this concession alone. Note, however, that this concession is confined to the conversion mechanism and does not authorize the companion cap reduction.
- Indemnification cap reduction: REJECT. The cap reduction is distinct from, and not covered by, the conceded basket conversion. Because Schedule 5.2's retained liabilities would be silently shifted by any reduction in the cap, the markup must be returned to the firm-standard cap. The cap reduction must be withdrawn. If the counterparty insists on a different cap, it must provide updated Schedule 5.2 disclosure and the client must receive corresponding consideration or risk-allocation relief before the term can be accepted. As drafted, the cap reduction is not acceptable.

II. MATERIAL ADVERSE EFFECT — REGULATORY-ACTION CARVE-OUTS

Deviation. The counterparty adds new carve-outs to the definition of Material Adverse Effect excluding regulatory action "of exactly the kind at issue in this matter."

Disclosure Schedule 3.7. Schedule 3.7 discloses two PENDING REGULATORY INQUIRIES that intersect precisely the regulatory-action carve-outs the counterparty proposes. Because the disclosed pending inquiries are of the same character as the action the carve-out would exclude, adopting the markup's carve-outs would carve out the very regulatory adverse effects that the parties knowingly allocated through the Schedule 3.7 disclosure. The scheduled exceptions control over the general statements in the base materials, and Schedule 3.7's disclosure is an operative representation that must remain enforceable.

Reconciliation and Recommendation: REJECT the MAE carve-outs as drafted. The carve-outs would strip MAE protection for the two pending regulatory inquiries disclosed in Schedule 3.7, defeating the purpose of the disclosure and materially shifting risk to the client. The definition of MAE must be restored to the firm-standard formulation so that regulatory action of the type disclosed in Schedule 3.7 continues to qualify as a Material Adverse Effect. If the counterparty seeks any regulatory-action protection, it must be narrowly drafted to exclude only future, undisclosed regulatory action of a general, prospective nature and must expressly not apply to the two pending inquiries already disclosed. Absent such a narrowed formulation, the carve-outs are a non-starter.

III. SURVIVAL PERIOD / LIMITATION-PERIOD CHANGE (Core Representations)

Deviation. The counterparty adds a new limitation period that shortens the survival of the core representations.

Exhibit B. Exhibit B sets the survival matrix for the agreement. The markup's limitation-period change directly contradicts the survival matrix in Exhibit B.

Deal-Team Instruction. The controlling correspondence states that the client treats ANY survival-period reduction as a WALK-AWAY issue. This priority supersedes the earlier, opposite ordering in the thread; only the latest message controls.

Reconciliation and Recommendation: WALK-AWAY ISSUE. The shortening of the survival period for the core representations is a walk-away term. It contradicts the Exhibit B survival matrix, and the client will not accept any reduction to the survival period. The counterparty's new limitation period must be withdrawn in its entirety and the survival period restored to match Exhibit B. This is not a negotiable point under the governing instruction; it is a condition to proceeding with the transaction.

ADDITIONAL RECONCILIATION NOTES

- Schedule-vs.-General-Precedence: Per the schedules, scheduled exceptions control over general statements in the base materials. All conclusions above honor that hierarchy, relying on Schedule 3.7 (pending regulatory inquiries), Schedule 5.2 (retained liabilities), and Exhibit B (survival matrix) as the operative controls.
- Bundled-Term Discipline: The concession of the basket conversion is strictly limited. It must not be treated as a concession of the companion cap reduction or of any other indemnification, MAE, or survival change. Each deviation is evaluated independently on its merits and under the governing priority.

RECOMMENDED RESPONSE POSTURE

1. ACCEPT — Basket conversion from deductible to tipping basket (stand-alone, per governing instruction).
2. REJECT — Indemnification cap reduction (Schedule 5.2 retained-liability shift; outside the conceded basket conversion).
3. REJECT — MAE carve-outs for regulatory action (schedule 3.7 pending inquiries; carve-outs would gut MAE protection).
4. WALK-AWAY — Survival-period / limitation-period reduction for core representations (contradicts Exhibit B; controlling instruction treats any reduction as a walk-away issue).

NEXT STEPS

Counsel to prepare a redline retracting the cap reduction, the MAE carve-outs, and the limitation-period change, while effecting the agreed basket conversion. The counterparty is to be put on notice that (a) the cap and MAE terms are not negotiable as drafted, and (b) the survival period is a walk-away item that must be restored to the Exhibit B matrix before the transaction can proceed.

This memorandum constitutes the redline review deliverable for Matter File 15.
